# Azure DevOps Resources

## MANDATORY WORKFLOW — follow this on every invocation

**Step 1 — Read the reference file.**
Before taking any action, you MUST read the relevant reference file(s) listed below. Do NOT skip this step or rely on prior knowledge.

**Step 2 — Use PowerShell scripts.**
All operations MUST be performed using the PowerShell scripts located in the `scripts/` subfolder of this skill. Direct `az` CLI commands are FORBIDDEN unless:
- no script exists for the required operation, **or**
- the user explicitly asks to use `az` CLI.

**Step 3 — Resolve configuration from AGENTS.md.**
Read the `azure-devops` section of the repository-wide `AGENTS.md` to get `organization`, `project`, `area-path`, and `iteration-path` before running any script.

---

## Prerequisites

Authentication (the scripts pick the first available option):

1. **Personal Access Token (preferred for CI/agents)** &mdash; set the environment variable `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` to a PAT with the required scopes (Work Items r/w, Code r/w, Pull Requests r/w). The `az devops/boards/repos` CLI honours this natively, and the PowerShell scripts in this skill switch to PAT Basic auth for direct REST calls when this variable is set. **No `az login` needed.** This is the path used by the Zephyr automation pods.
2. **Azure CLI interactive login (local dev)** &mdash; `az login` (or `az login --use-device-code`). The scripts fall back to `az account get-access-token` when `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` is not set.

In both cases:

- Azure CLI (`az`) must be installed.
- The `azure-devops` extension is required: `az extension add --name azure-devops`.

> **Never** trigger `az login --use-device-code` from inside an automated agent run &mdash; it will block the pod waiting for human input. If you see the scripts failing because no token is available, set `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` rather than logging in interactively.
